title: Import, export and back up
p: Your notes should never be locked inside an app. Import Markdown or Feishu DocxXML, export a page as PDF or Markdown, and back up your documents as an ordinary folder.
Choose the import command in the File menu, or press ⌘ ⇧ I. Select one or more files. Each file becomes a new document; the last imported one opens when the import finishes.

td.p: Headings, lists, tasks, code, tables, links and supported image references become editable blocks.
Text is imported with Markdown input supported by the importer.
Supported rich text, callouts, columns, tables and inline objects are preserved.

ul.li: The filename supplies the document title. A matching first Markdown heading is not repeated in the body.
Local Markdown images referenced by relative or file URLs are copied into your documents folder.
An unreadable or unsupported file produces an import error; existing notes are not replaced.

callout.p: You can also paste into an existing page. Structured content preserves supported formatting; Markdown text is converted. Use ⌘ ⇧ V for plain text.

p: Open the document's More menu or right-click its sidebar entry and choose a download format.
PDF export lays out the page for A4 paper and preserves document styling, images and tables. Use it for sharing a read-only copy or checking a print layout.

column.p: Export a single Markdown file without copying images or attachments.
Export the Markdown file alongside an assets folder. Image and attachment links use relative paths.

p: Some rich layouts have no exact Markdown equivalent:

td.p: Blockquotes beginning with the callout icon
Pipe-separated tables; multiple cell paragraphs use line breaks
Content written in sequence rather than side by side
Not all styling is representable; use PDF when appearance matters

p: Use the print command from the document menu to open the system print dialog. Choose a printer there, or save a PDF.
The default location is ~/Documents/Quiet.md. Settings › Documents shows the folder location.

pre.caption: ~/Documents/Quiet.md
pre.code: Quiet.md/ ├── docs/ One XML file per document ├── assets/ Images and attachments ├── themes/ Custom CSS themes ├── trash/ Deleted documents ├── index.json Hierarchy, pins, favorites and dates ├── preferences.json Theme and language preferences └── shortcuts.json Custom keyboard shortcuts

p: Document files use DocxXML. You can inspect them with a text editor, but quit the app before editing files in your documents folder externally.

ul.li: Autosave: edits are written after a short pause. A temporary file is written before replacing the document.
Visible errors: failed saves remain marked as unsaved. Before switching documents or quitting, the app asks how to handle them.
Index backup: index.json.bak helps recover an unreadable index.

Multiple windows: windows in the same app process share changes. Independent instances check the saved document against the version they opened. A conflicting save is rejected instead of overwriting newer content; export your unsaved work before reopening.

p: Include the entire documents folder, not just the XML files. Time Machine can protect it if the Documents folder is included in your backup. For a manual archive, quit Quiet.md and run:
A sync service is not a substitute for a backup. Avoid editing the same synced documents on two computers at once; local file locking does not coordinate separate machines.

ol.li: Quit Quiet.md on the old Mac with ⌘ Q.
Copy the complete Quiet.md folder into Documents on the new Mac.
Open Quiet.md there. The folder includes your documents, hierarchy, themes and shortcuts.

callout.p: DocxXML files placed directly in your documents folder’s docs subfolder are also discovered. Keep a backup before doing a bulk import this way.
